LESSON: RHYTHM

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one
Subject: CREATIVE ACTIVITIES FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Creating and Execution
Topic 1.7: Rhythm
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 14

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Rhythm, part of Creating and Execution in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one CREATIVE ACTIVITIES FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: How can different body percussion be used to accompany songs?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Rhythm together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and Imagination: The learner uses and explores their parts of the body to create rhythmic accompaniments to various songs.

• Learning to learn: The learner learns new ways to use body movements to maintain the beat outside the class alone or with others.

• Digital literacy: The learner interacts with a digital device to record the improvised body percussion accompaniments to the songs sung.

Values:
• Social Justice: The learner improvises rhythmic accompaniment using body percussion to songs from diverse Kenyan communities

developing a sense of diverse cultural awareness.

• Responsibility: The learner sings songs and takes turns to accompany others with body percussion to maintain rhythm.

• Unity: The learner plays the recorded performance and gives positive feedback to others.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Peace Education: The learner sings familiar topical songs that convey peace messages.

Link to other learning areas:

• Mathematics Activities: The learner applies the skill of counting to maintain beat when practicing performing various body percussions.

Suggested learning resources:

Open safe quiet space, digital devices: laptops, tablets, smart phones, computers, hearing aids, Body percussions, Percussion instruments,

whistles, whiskers assorted sound instruments or objects, musical instruments, reference books, virtual sites, resource person
